statement: Let r ≥ 0 and n ≥ 1, and let k1, . . . , kr be positive integers. For each j ∈ {1, . . . , n}, let Bj be a finite ordered list of pairs (i, s) with 1 ≤ i ≤ r and s ∈ {1, −1}; repetitions are allowed. Set dj = X (i,s)∈Bj ki, bij = X (i′,s)∈Bj i′=i s, B = (bij). 3 Suppose that B has row rank r over Q. For arbitrary Pj ∈ U(dj), define D = r Y i=1 U(ki), Fj(X) = diag(i,s)∈Bj (Xs i )Pj (X ∈ D). Then there is X ∈ D such that n X j=1 dimC ker(Fj(X) − Idj ) ≥ r X i=1 ki. (2.1) Here U(0) and an empty product of groups are points, and the fixed-space dimension in dimension zero is zero.
